en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 9.5.
Hetuduka, Sanidassanattika

Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor non-visible-and-reactive, there arises a state that is neither a root-cause nor non-visible-and-reactive by way of the root-cause condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor non-visible-and-reactive, [there arises] a state that is not a root-cause...
A state that is neither-root, non-visible, and impinging arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-root, non-visible, and impinging, there arise states that are both neither-root and non-visible-impinging, as well as states that are neither-root and not non-visible-impinging, by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not-root-conditioned, not-visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is not-root-conditioned, not-visible, and impinging, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is not-root-conditioned, not-visible, and impinging, there arises a state that is not-root-conditioned, not-visible, and impinging, by way of root condition. [Dependent on] a state that is not-root-conditioned, not-visible, and impinging...
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor visible-with-resistance, states that are neither roots nor visible-with-resistance arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor visible-with-resistance and a state that is neither a root nor visible-with-resistance...
A state that is neither-root, not-visible, and impinging arises by way of root-condition from a state that is neither-root, not-visible, and impinging.

A state that is neither-root, not-visible, and impinging arises by way of root-condition dependent on both a state that is neither-root, not-visible, and impinging, and a state that is neither-root, not-visible, and impinging. [A state that is] neither-root, not-visible, and impinging, and [a state that is] neither-root, not-visible, and impinging...
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor visible nor impinging, states that are neither roots nor visible nor impinging arise by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of root; ... pe ... nine in the case of non-disappearance. (Nine in all instances.)
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor non-demonstrative-and-reactive, there arises a state that is neither-root nor non-demonstrative-and-reactive by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor non-demonstrative-and-reactive, there arises a state that is not-neither-root nor non-demonstrative-and-reactive by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor non-demonstrative-and-reactive, there arises a state that is neither-root... [and so forth].
Conditioned by states that are neither-root nor visible-with-resistance, states that are neither-root nor visible-with-resistance arise by way of root-condition.
Conditioned by a state that is neither-root nor visible-with-resistance, a state that is neither-root nor visible-with-resistance arises by way of root-condition.
Conditioned by a state that is neither-root nor visible-with-resistance, a state that is with-root... [arises].
A state that is neither visible nor impinging arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is neither a root,

neither visible, nor impinging, there arise states that are neither roots, neither visible, nor impinging, and states that are neither roots but are neither visible nor impinging, by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-rooted, non-visible, and non-reactive, and a state that is neither-rooted, non-visible, and non-reactive, there arises a state that is neither-rooted, non-visible, and non-reactive by way of root condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-rooted, non-visible, and non-reactive, and a state that is neither-rooted, non-visible, and non-reactive, there arises a state that is neither-rooted, non-visible, and non-reactive... [and so forth].

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor non-demonstrable-and-reactive, and [a state] that is neither-root nor non-demonstrable-and-reactive, there arise states that are neither-root nor non-demonstrable-and-reactive and states that are neither-root nor non-demonstrable-and-reactive by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the root condition (*hetu-paccaya*), there are nine [answers] …pe… in the non-disappearance condition (*avigata-paccaya*), there are nine. (The detailed exposition applies everywhere in the co-nascent section …pe… and in the associated section.

Root-object condition (*hetu-ārammaṇa-paccaya*): A state that is not a root, is non-demonstrable, and possesses resistance (*na-anahetu na-anidassana-sappaṭigho dhammo*) is related to a state that is not a root, is non-demonstrable, and possesses resistance.

Condition by way of root-cause (hetu-paccaya). A state that is not-root-cause (na-hetu), not-visible (na-anidassana), and impinging (sappaṭigha) is a condition by way of root-cause for a state that is not-root-cause, not-visible, and impinging.

A state that is not-root-cause, not-visible, and impinging is a condition by way of root-cause for a state that is both not-root-cause, not-visible, and impinging, and for a state that is not-root-cause, not-visible, and impinging [as its concomitant].

A state that is neither a cause nor non-visible-and-reactive is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is neither a cause nor non-visible-and-reactive. (Abbreviated. Under the heading of cause, three;
under object, nine … pe … under decisive support, nine; under prenascence and postnascence, three;
under repetition, nine; under kamma, three; under result, nine; under nutriment, three; under faculty, nine; under jhāna, three; under path and association, [three].
Nine, five in dissociation … pe … nine in non-disappearance. (The Chapter of Questions should be expanded in this manner.

Dependent on a state that is not a root, not visible, and not impinging, there arises a state that is not a root, not visible, and not impinging, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of root: one;
in predominance, conascence, mutuality, dependence, kamma … pe … path: one; in dissociation, presence, and non-disappearance: one. (Full expansion for all cases.)
